title: SOROBALTE – Discover Riga and Latvia
desc: Guide and travel support for Riga and Latvia: tours, accommodation, food and traditions.
hero_h: Riga and Latvia, on the Baltic shore
hero_p: An Art Nouveau capital, endless forests, white sand beaches and living traditions. We help you discover them.
riga_p1: Founded in 1201, Riga is the largest city in the Baltic states. Its old town has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997, with medieval lanes, guild halls and church spires.
riga_p2: It also has one of Europe’s finest Art Nouveau districts, around Alberta Street, and a vast market housed in former zeppelin hangars.
lv_p: The country is small, flat and green: two hours from Riga, the scenery changes completely.
lv1_d: Sandstone cliffs, medieval castles and trails in the country’s oldest national park.
lv2_d: A long fine-sand beach and 19th-century wooden villas, 30 minutes from Riga.
lv3_d: Old town on the UNESCO list since 2023 and the Venta waterfall, Europe’s widest at about 250 m.
exp1_d: Two hours between Town Hall Square, the cathedral and hidden courtyards.
exp2_d: Carved façades on Alberta Street and a visit to a period apartment.
exp3_d: Taste rye bread, cheeses, smoked fish and seasonal berries.
exp4_d: A day trip to the baroque palace and its French-style gardens.
stay_p: A simple selection to fit your budget and pace.
stay1_d: Walk everywhere, in renovated historic buildings.
stay2_d: Quiet, sauna and local breakfast, in Jūrmala or along the coast.
stay3_d: Family welcome, farm produce and forest walks.
food1_d: Rupjmaize, dark and dense, goes with almost every meal. It also makes a dessert, rupjmaizes kārtojums (pictured).
food2_d: A traditional winter dish served with onion and kefir.
food3_d: June 23–24: flower crowns, bonfires, songs and caraway cheese.
srv1_d: A plan built around your dates, budget and interests.
srv2_d: Guided tours in Riga and small-group excursions.
srv3_d: Accommodation, transport and activities arranged for you.

faq1_a: May to September for beaches and long days. Midsummer (Jāņi) is on June 23–24. Winters are cold, with lovely Christmas markets in Riga.
faq2_a: Latvia uses the euro and is part of the Schengen area: EU citizens can travel with an ID card.
faq3_a: Latvian is the official language. English is common in tourism and Russian is widely spoken.
faq4_q: How do I get from the airport to the centre?
faq4_a: Riga airport is about 10 km from the centre. A bus, taxi or ride-hailing car reaches the Old Town in 20 to 30 minutes.
exp5_d: Where the Baltic Sea meets the Gulf of Riga, at the northern tip of Courland.
exp6_d: A west-coast port city and the former naval district of Karosta, with its Orthodox cathedral.
exp7_d: A medieval fortress on the Daugava, now the president’s residence.
exp8_d: The last surviving city gate, cut through the walls in 1698.

d1_d: Morning in the Old Town (Town Hall Square, cathedral, Swedish Gate). Lunch at the Central Market, then Alberta Street and its Art Nouveau façades.
d2_d: Train to Majori (about 30 minutes), the beach, pedestrian Jomas iela and wooden villas.
d3_d: Turaida Castle, the Gauja valley and trails, then back to Riga by train or bus (about 75 minutes).
s1_d: Parks turn green and the Venta is at its widest during the snowmelt.
s2_d: Jūrmala beaches, very short nights and Midsummer on June 23–24.
s3_d: Russet forests in the Gauja, mushrooms and berries, markets full of flavour.
s4_d: Christmas markets, sauna and snow: Riga lights up and days are short.
exp9_d: Medieval castle ruins and a quiet old town in Gauja National Park.
exp10_d: A tribute to soldiers killed in the War of Independence, unveiled in 1935 and now a national symbol.
h2: Riga joins the Hanseatic League and trades across Northern Europe.
h3: First great song festival, a tradition still alive today.
h5: Independence is restored after Soviet occupation.
h6: Latvia joins NATO, then the European Union.
h7: Riga is European Capital of Culture and Latvia adopts the euro.
h8: Kuldīga’s old town joins the UNESCO list.
song_p: Since 1873, thousands of singers and dancers have gathered roughly every five years. The tradition is recognised by UNESCO; around 500,000 visitors were expected in 2018. The great stage at Mežaparks in Riga has hosted it since 1955.
food4_d: A dark, bitter herbal liqueur made in Riga since 1752, drunk as a digestif or in coffee.
food5_d: Smoked herring, sprats and eel, to taste at the Central Market with rye bread.
faq5_q: Can I manage without a car?
faq5_a: Yes for Riga, which is easy on foot. Trains link Riga with Jūrmala and Sigulda; a car is still useful for the countryside and the west coast.
